source_data_vintage_statement: official archive retrieved 2026-08-26; embedded shapefile members dated 2019-11; provider does not expose a formal release identifier in the archive name
attribution: Instituto Geográfico Nacional de la República Argentina (IGN)
license_evidence: IGN's current Capas SIG surface makes the Departamento vector layer available for download. Current IGN demarcation metadata states free use with appropriate citation of IGN. The repository re-fetches the official archive and verifies its exact SHA-256 rather than redistributing the archive.
identity_note: IN1 is the complete five-digit administrative code in the exact archive and is unique for all 529 features. OBJECTID is also complete and unique and is preserved as a source feature identifier. Names are not unique and are never used as identity.

corroborating_wfs.identity_note: The WFS corroborates the currently served department layer and IN1-like administrative identity, but repeated WFS serialization is not byte-stable and therefore is not the release anchor.

known_limitations: The exact release anchor is the byte-stable official SHAPE archive retrieved on 2026-08-26, not a claim that the embedded geometry was authored in 2026. Archive members carry November 2019 timestamps and the provider does not expose a formal immutable release identifier in the filename.
The current live WFS serves a related 529-feature department layer but repeated responses are not byte-identical; WFS evidence is therefore corroborating rather than the release identity.
The layer contains Departamento, Partido and Comuna labels under one second-order administrative layer; the source vocabulary is preserved rather than collapsed.
The source extent includes Argentina's bicontinental/Antarctic representation to latitude -90. A Census relation is expected to leave administrative targets outside Census coverage unreferenced.
SAG and FDC preserve heterogeneous upstream lineage/capture information. FDC is missing for most archive rows; no uniform provenance is inferred from those fields.
Administrative names are not unique. Consumers must use native_id/IN1 or geo_uid, not FNA/NAM, for identity.
This release does not assert that IGN administrative geometry supersedes, repairs or replaces Census statistical geography.
